Synthetic example data in the shape of published tables

Source: R/sfx.R
synfix.Rd

Draws a data frame with the columns of a published administrative table and values of the kinds it holds, for examples, tests and teaching where the real table cannot be shipped or fetched. Each column is drawn on its own, uniformly from its values: nothing in the result is a record of anyone, and no relation between columns is kept.

Usage

synfix(kind = NULL, n = 100, seed = 1)

Arguments

kind

The name of a preset or of a family of presets, a named list of the values of each column, or NULL for the list of presets.

n

The number of rows: one whole number from 1 to 1e7.

seed

The seed: one whole number from 0 to 2147483647.

Value

A data frame of n rows; for a family, a named list of them (named "a01", ..., or "incidents", ...); for kind = NULL, a data frame with one row per column of every preset: kind, column, type ("labels", "range" or "id") and values (the labels separated by "|", or the ends of the range).

Details

A preset gives the columns of one table: the Ontario corrections tables on segregation, restrictive confinement and deaths in custody ("otis-a01", "otis-b01" to "otis-b09", "otis-c01" to "otis-c12", "otis-d01" to "otis-d07") and on use of force in correctional institutions ("cuof-incidents", "cuof-incident_type", "cuof-indigenous", "cuof-inmate_incident", "cuof-inmate_participant", "cuof-institution_summary", "cuof-location_summary", "cuof-race", "cuof-ethnic_origin", "cuof-religion", "cuof-select_incident_summary", "cuof-staff_incident"). A column of a preset takes one of a set of labels, a whole number from a range, or a synthetic identifier ("syn-00001" to "syn-" and max(2, n %/% 4) in five digits, so that identifiers repeat as people's do). "otis" or "cuof" alone gives the list of every table of the family, the i-th drawn with the seed (seed + i) %% 2^31. kind = NULL lists the presets.

Any other table is a named list, one element per column, each a vector of the values the column takes (labels or numbers), drawn with replacement; a value given once is a constant column.

The draws are those of R's sample.int(m, n, replace = TRUE) after set.seed(seed), made by the package's own copy of R's generator, so the result is the same on every system and in every language, and the session's random numbers are not touched.

Examples

head(synfix("otis-b02", n = 20, seed = 3))
#>   EndFiscalYear UniqueIndividual_ID Gender Region_MostRecentPlacement
#> 1          2022           syn-00002 Female                    Toronto
#> 2          2019           syn-00001 Female                    Central
#> 3          2021           syn-00004 Female                    Western
#> 4          2024           syn-00004 Female                    Eastern
#> 5          2021           syn-00003   Male                    Western
#> 6          2019           syn-00002   Male                    Eastern
#>   Age_Category TotalAggregatedDays_Segregation
#> 1          50+                              57
#> 2     18 to 24                              76
#> 3     18 to 24                               8
#> 4     25 to 49                              49
#> 5          50+                              54
#> 6     18 to 24                              44
x <- synfix("cuof", n = 5)
names(x)
#>  [1] "incidents"               "incident_type"          
#>  [3] "indigenous"              "inmate_incident"        
#>  [5] "inmate_participant"      "institution_summary"    
#>  [7] "location_summary"        "race"                   
#>  [9] "ethnic_origin"           "religion"               
#> [11] "select_incident_summary" "staff_incident"         
synfix(list(year = 2019:2023, sex = c("F", "M")), n = 4, seed = 9)
#>   year sex
#> 1 2021   F
#> 2 2023   M
#> 3 2021   M
#> 4 2021   F
head(synfix())
#>       kind                     column   type
#> 1 otis-a01              EndFiscalYear  range
#> 2 otis-a01        UniqueIndividual_ID     id
#> 3 otis-a01   Region_AtTimeOfPlacement labels
#> 4 otis-a01 Region_MostRecentPlacement labels
#> 5 otis-a01                     Gender labels
#> 6 otis-a01               Age_Category labels
#>                                     values
#> 1                                2018|2024
#> 2                                         
#> 3 Central|Eastern|Northern|Toronto|Western
#> 4 Central|Eastern|Northern|Toronto|Western
#> 5                              Female|Male
#> 6                    18 to 24|25 to 49|50+
